original_question: Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, µ, S), a number of colors r, and a threshold λ in the measure range, calculate the (r, λ)-centerpole number c_r^λ(X), meaning the smallest size of a subfamily S' ⊂ S such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a monochromatic S'-symmetric measurable set of measure at least λ.
target_in_paper: Section 10, Problem 10.1, together with the definition immediately preceding it of an (r, λ)-centerpole subfamily and the number c_r^λ(X).
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the right part of the paper: the Section 10 notion of an (r, λ)-centerpole number for a symmetry measure space X = (X, μ, S). It also correctly captures the core minimization problem: find the smallest subfamily S' ⊂ S such that every measurable r-coloring of X contains a monochromatic measurable subset of measure at least λ that is symmetric with respect to some symmetry from S'.
missing_details: In the paper, r is a cardinal, not just a finite number of colors.
The threshold λ is not merely a real number in a measure range; it is an element of the complete linearly ordered value set in which μ takes values.

A symmetry measure space X = (X, μ, S) has specific built-in hypotheses: μ is a monotone measure defined on a σ-algebra of subsets of X, and S is a family of bijective measure-preserving transformations that is closed under inverses.
The phrase "S'-symmetric" must be made precise: a measurable set A is S'-symmetric if A = s(A) for some s in S', not necessarily for every s in S'.
A measurable r-coloring means that each color class is μ-measurable.
The paper explicitly defines c_r^λ(X) as the minimal cardinality of such a subfamily; if no such subfamily exists, one sets c_r^λ(X) = ∞.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the quantifiers should be explicit: determine c_r^λ(X) for a given symmetry measure space X, for each cardinal r and each λ in the value set of μ.
The draft states the definition but not quite the official problem statement, which is to calculate these numbers for the given symmetry measure space.
refined_question: Given a symmetry measure space X = (X, μ, S), where μ is a monotone measure on a σ-algebra of subsets of X with values in a complete linearly ordered set and S is a family of bijective μ-preserving admissible symmetries of X, determine for each cardinal r and each λ in the value set of μ the (r, λ)-centerpole number c_r^λ(X): the least cardinality of a subfamily S' ⊂ S such that every measurable r-coloring χ : X → r (that is, each color class χ^{-1}(i) is μ-measurable) contains a monochromatic measurable set A ⊂ X with μ(A) ≥ λ and A = s(A) for some s ∈ S'; if no such subfamily exists, set c_r^λ(X) = ∞.
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's Section 10 centerpole-number problem, not at the earlier maximal-symmetry-number material. The exact official formulation is Problem 10.1, which asks to calculate the (r, λ)-centerpole numbers of a symmetry measure space. The sentence immediately before Problem 10.1 gives the precise definition of an (r, λ)-centerpole subfamily and of c_r^λ(X), and Sections 2 and 3 supply the hidden technical meanings of "symmetry measure space," "measurable coloring," and "symmetric subset." The paper then notes that its concrete partial answers are mainly for Euclidean spaces R^n and discrete subspaces Z^n equipped with asymptotic-dimension measure, mostly in the case λ = 0, so the general Section 10 problem is the narrowest paper-faithful target that matches your draft.
